nameOrigin.text: Joseph Selig suggested the name after a favorite character in Sir Walter Scott's novel The Legend of Montrose.

founded.text: Officially became a town; the first stake was driven in December 1881

timeline.text: The Ute Indians were relocated to a reservation in Utah in September, and the first stake of the town was driven in December.
Montrose officially became a town, and the Denver and Rio Grande Railroad built its narrow gauge mainline through it.
The Gunnison Tunnel, built to bring irrigation water to the Uncompahgre Valley, opened with a visit from President Taft.
The Ute Indian Museum was built near the ranch of Uncompahgre leader Chief Ouray and his wife Chipeta.
